extracted.intended_audience: legal scholars, empirical researchers, and policy analysts studying patent litigation and patent-system outcomes
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for coding patent litigation docket events and merits decisions for an empirical dataset, including unit of observation, inclusion/exclusion rules, issue-level coding of outcomes, technology and industry classification, and modeling choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of observation / claim-level granularity
rubrics_metrics.description: We created a new record for each group of claims that had a different substantive outcome, thus taking the unit of observation down from the level of the patent to the level of the individual claim or group of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occasionally the court ruled differently on different claims of a patent (e.g., first claim infringed and not invalid, second claim not infringed and anticipated); in such cases generate separate observations per distinct substantive outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of decisions on a patent in a lawsuit
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, we treated a decision on a patent in a lawsuit as a single observation even if the patent was asserted against multiple parties in the same suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple parties are involved in the same suit asserting the same patent, treat the patent-level decision as one observation unless claim-level substantive outcomes differ (see Unit of observation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/exclusion of non-patent-specific rulings
rubrics_metrics.description: Excluded rulings on issues that were not patent specific, such as laches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not code rulings that do not pertain to patent law substantive issues (e.g., equitable defenses) as patent merits rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of summary judgment motions
rubrics_metrics.description: We excluded summary judgment rulings on patent-law issues if the court did not reach the merits of those issues—such as denials of summary judgment motions on the grounds that they were premature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial of summary judgment does not result in a final resolution; denial = unresolved disputed issue of material fact. If summary judgment is granted on an issue, code the summary judgment ruling as the final resolution; if denied and later resolved at trial, use the trial resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of trial outcomes and post-verdict motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Coders reviewed and recorded all trial outcomes, whether there was a jury or bench trial, as well as decisions on post-verdict motions for judgment as a matter of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record jury vs bench trial status and any post-verdict JMOL dispositions when determining final resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and appellate resolution coding
rubrics_metrics.description: We recorded whether an appeal was lodged, and how the appeal was resolved (affirmed, reversed, pending, or dismissed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the underlying trial or appellate court opinion lacked sufficient detail to ascertain the basis for the ruling, read the underlying briefing by the parties. If the Federal Circuit reversed a ruling, update the final-resolution coding to reflect the appellate decision; retain original decision in summary-judgment coding to capture trial-court summary judgment win rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merits-issue-level coding (invalidity grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: For invalidity, we coded whether the ruling was based on utility, patentable subject matter, § 102 prior art, obviousness, indefiniteness, written description, enablement, or best mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also code various bases for § 102 invalidity separately. Include merits rulings on each distinct issue litigated to decision, even if multiple issues were raised and decided differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merits-issue-level coding (infringement)
rubrics_metrics.description: For infringement, we captured literal infringement, the doctrine of equivalents, and various types of indirect infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When indirect infringement is asserted, code the specific type (e.g., inducement, contributory) where ascertainable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merits-issue-level coding (unenforceability)
rubrics_metrics.description: We coded unenforceability, as well as the basis for the unenforceability argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the specific basis (e.g., inequitable conduct, fraud) when a court rules on unenforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitive wins vs interim wins
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions that finally ruled for a party on an issue were coded as definitive wins, and decisions that ruled for a party but kept the issue alive (largely denials of summary judgment but also remands on appeal) were coded as interim wins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this distinction to separate final, dispositive outcomes from temporary or non-final favorable rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology-area assignment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigned each patent in the study to a single, primary technology area (six primary areas) and, in about one-third of patents, one or more secondary technology areas when another area clearly formed an additional but integral part of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place emphasis on the claims, aided by written descriptions and drawings to explain ambiguous claim terms; consult technical dictionaries/encyclopedias/Internet only when further interpretation is required; primary areas are mutually exclusive while primary-plus-secondary are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of primary technology areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology areas defined as: (1) Mechanical, (2) Electrical, (3) Chemistry, (4) Biotechnology, (5) Software, (6) Optics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the original text definitions (e.g., Mechanical: claims cover use of mechanical parts; Software: claims cover data processing—the actual manipulation of data—and not merely transmission/receipt/storage; Biotechnology: advanced genetic techniques, products created by such processes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Software business-method subset definition and modeling guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Software business-method category includes software patents that cover models, methods, and techniques for conducting business transactions (narrow definition: automated financial generation of customer proposals, advertising techniques, online catalogs); excludes computer-controlled manufacturing methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because business-method is a subset of software, do not include the software superset and all of its subsets in the same regression specification; adopt one model with the software superset and a separate model with the two mutually exclusive subsets (business-method and non-business-method) when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-category assignment procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry categories focused on the business use of the patent; assignment paid attention to claim language but relied more on the written description and extrinsic evidence (especially from the Internet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry categorization may require consulting extrinsic sources to determine the patent owner's industry or the way the technology is put to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of industry categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigned patents to one of eleven mutually exclusive industry categories: (1) Computer and Other Electronics, (2) Semiconductor, (3) Pharmaceutical, (4) Medical Devices, Methods, and Other Medical, (5) Biotechnology, (6) Communications, (7) Transportation (including automotive), (8) Construction, (9) Energy, (10) Goods and Services for Consumer Uses, (11) Goods and Services for Industrial and Business Uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the article's detailed category descriptions (e.g., Pharmaceutical includes drugs and processes for producing/using such drugs; Biotechnology industry includes inventions that advance the science of biotechnology rather than producing pharmaceutical compositions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and temporal limitations of the dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset limited to lawsuits filed January 1, 2008 through December 31, 2009; contains only patents subject to a ruling on summary judgment, a trial, or an appeal; cases settled before any substantive patent ruling are absent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize lack of generalizability to cases that settled without a merits ruling and that litigation/settlement incentives may bias observed win rates in unknown directions; interpret subgroup statistics cautiously due to smaller cell sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical modeling choices and remedies for non-independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Used logistic regression because dependent variables (specific outcomes) are binary; to remedy lack of independence among observations, simultaneously clustered standard errors on both unique patent numbers and cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for non-independence include multiple patents asserted in a case, same patent litigated in multiple suits, and consolidated cases; cluster on patents and cases in regressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding of summary-judgment vs final-resolution variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Final-resolution variables reflect trial or granted summary judgment outcomes; summary-judgment grants were coded as final resolutions, while denials alone were not final unless later resolved at trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain original summary-judgment coding even if appellate reversal occurs, but update final-resolution coding to reflect appellate outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of underlying party briefing when opinions lack detail
rubrics_metrics.description: When the underlying trial or appellate court opinion lacked sufficient detail to ascertain the basis for the ruling, we read the underlying briefing by the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult briefs and other primary docket materials to disambiguate the court's basis for a ruling when the opinion is silent or vague.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and interpretation of observed win rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported win rates are for cases that reached a definitive outcome; because most lawsuits settle before any ruling on the merits, the data cannot tell us who would win cases that are filed but settled without any substantive ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid extrapolating these win rates to all filed cases or to unlitigated disputes; consider selection effects and confidentiality of settlements when interpreting the direction of bias.
